name: Kanakangi
description: The first raga of the entire system  ·  sparse, primordial, rarely performed. Its two consecutive lower notes give it a stark, almost primeval quality.

name: Ratnangi
description: Subtle and inward-looking. The flat lower register and muted upper notes create a contemplative, almost wordless quality.

name: Ganamurti
description: Named for Ganapati (Gana + murti), suggesting auspicious beginnings. The bright Ni3 over the flat lower register creates a striking contrast.

name: Vanaspati
description: Evokes the quiet of a forest  ·  flat lower notes, gentle upper register. Rarely heard, but carries a sense of deep natural stillness.

name: Manavati
description: A raga of quiet dignity. The flat Ri against the bright upper notes gives it a solemn, unhurried feeling.

name: Tanarupi
description: One of the most structurally unusual Melakartas  ·  it skips Da entirely, leaping from Pa straight to Ni2. The consecutive Ni2-Ni3 in the upper register creates a tense, contemplative quality.

name: Senavati
description: The flat Ri and Ga2 lower tetrachord, combined with flat Da, gives this raga a grounded, unhurried devotional quality.

name: Hanumatodi
description: The parent of Todi  ·  one of the most beloved ragas in all of Carnatic music. Its deeply flat lower register holds you gently in longing. Morning performances are legendary.

name: Dhenuka
description: The sharp Ni3 over the deeply flat lower register creates an unexpected brightness  ·  like sunlight breaking through an overcast morning.

name: Natakapriya
description: Dramatic contrast between flat lower and middle register. Said to be suited for theatrical expression.

name: Kokilapriya
description: Named for the koel (kokila). The flat lower register with a bright Da2-Ni3 upper tetrachord creates something lovely and surprising.

name: Rupavati
description: Two consecutive upper semitones against the flat lower tetrachord. An unusual structural symmetry that gives it a reflective, aesthetic quality.

name: Gayakapriya
description: The combination of flat Ri with natural Ga3 is a signature sound  ·  warm and earnest. The flat Da cluster gives a tender quality.

name: Vakulabharanam
description: A raga of tender devotion  ·  flat Ri and Da against natural Ga. Rarely explored fully but carries a distinctive sweetness.

name: Mayamalavagowla
description: The raga of morning prayers  ·  ancient, majestic, complete. Every music student's first Melakarta. The symmetry of Ri1/Da1 with Ga3/Ni3 gives it an eternal, timeless feeling.

name: Chakravakam
description: Parent of the beloved janya Chakravakam  ·  gentle and warm. The natural Ga with moderate upper notes creates a calm, even temperament.

name: Suryakantam
description: Named for the sun  ·  the flat Ri against a bright upper tetrachord gives a luminous quality, like sunlight on still water.

name: Hatakambari
description: The consecutive Ni2-Ni3 in the upper register creates an unusual intensity. The combination with natural Ga is striking and memorable.

name: Jhankaradhwani
description: The Da1-Da2 cluster in the upper register gives it an unusual resonant quality, like temple bells with a slight shadow.

name: Natabhairavi
description: The mother of Bhairavi and parent to an entire universe of melancholic ragas. Vast, maternal, emotionally complete. Singing Natabhairavi feels like being held.

name: Keeravani
description: The same as a natural minor scale with sharp seventh  ·  strikingly close to Western harmonic minor. It has a quality of yearning that resolves into wonder.

name: Kharaharapriya
description: The "everyman's raga"  ·  widely loved, sung in homes and concert halls alike. Its gentle, natural quality makes it feel like being understood. Parent of Abheri, Nayaki, and many more.

name: Gowrimanohari
description: Named for Gauri (Parvati). The flat Ga against bright Da2-Ni3 creates an elegant, feminine quality  ·  graceful and devotional.

name: Varunapriya
description: Named for Varuna, god of waters. The flowing consecutive upper semitones suggest water in motion  ·  deep below, moving above.

name: Mararanjani
description: The bright natural Ga3 with Ri2 in the lower register and the unusual Da cluster gives a surprisingly playful, cheerful feeling.

name: Charukesi
description: An extraordinary raga  ·  bright Ga3 shadowed by flat Da1 and Ni2. It feels like courage in the face of loss, or joy carrying grief within it. One of the most emotionally complex Melakartas.

name: Sarasangi
description: Natural Ga3 and Ni3 with flat Da1 creates a distinctive gentle tension. Clear and devotional in character.

name: Harikambhoji
description: One of the most generative Melakartas  ·  parent to Kamboji, Mohanam, Khamas, Bilahari, and dozens of other beloved janyas. Rich, warm, and welcoming.

name: Dheerasankarabharanam
description: All natural notes  ·  the "Western Major scale" of Carnatic music. Universally loved, capable of expressing the entire range of human emotion. Tyagaraja's most triumphant compositions live here.

name: Naganandini
description: Named for the divine serpent. The consecutive upper semitones feel sinuous and hypnotic, moving in ways you don't quite expect.

name: Yagapriya
description: The R5 rows begin with Ga2 (Ri3) where Ri would normally be  ·  giving a strikingly compressed lower register. Named for fire rituals (yagas), it has an ancient, ceremonial quality.

name: Ragavardhini
description: Named "raga-increaser"  ·  as if it contains within it the seed of all ragas. The compressed lower tetrachord against a gentle upper register has unexpected richness.

name: Gangeyabhushani
description: Named for the ornament of the Ganges  ·  the sharp Ni3 over flat Da1, combined with the consecutive lower Ga notes, gives it a sacred, flowing quality.

name: Vagadheeswari
description: Named for Saraswati, goddess of speech and learning. Its even temperament and balanced notes suggest eloquence and knowledge.

name: Shulini
description: Named for Shiva's trident  ·  the bright upper tetrachord with the compressed lower register creates something powerful and incisive.

name: Chalanata
description: The final Ma1 Melakarta  ·  named for movement in dance. Consecutive semitones in both lower and upper registers create a distinctive stepping quality.

name: Salagam
description: The sharp Ma2 against flat Ri and flat Da creates a gravity and depth that feels different from its Ma1 counterparts. The beginning of the Prati Madhyamam half.

name: Jalarnavam
description: Named "ocean of water"  ·  the Ma2 gives a sense of vastness and depth that the flat surrounding notes make feel even more spacious.

name: Jhalavarali
description: An unusual combination  ·  flat lower notes with sharp Ma2 and natural Ni3. Rarely performed but carries a sense of great antiquity.

name: Navaneetam
description: Named for fresh butter (navaneetam)  ·  soft and smooth. The Ma2 brings sharpness to an otherwise gentle raga.

name: Pavani
description: Named for purity and the wind. The Ma2 with bright upper notes brings a clear, airy quality despite the flat lower register.

name: Raghupriya
description: Named "dear to Raghu" (an epithet of Rama). Consecutive semitone pairs in both tetrachords with sharp Ma  ·  structurally unique and surprisingly stately.

name: Gavambhodi
description: Flat Ri, flat Ga, and flat Da against the sharp Ma  ·  an unusual mix that creates deep introspection and a sense of searching.

name: Bhavapriya
description: Named "dear to emotions." The Ma2 brings an elevated longing to the otherwise plaintive flat notes  ·  like yearning for something transcendent.

name: Shubhapantuvarali
description: Deep, ancient, almost Sanskrit in its seriousness. Flat Ri, Ga, Da against sharp Ma and Ni3  ·  a combination that feels like it comes from another era. Rare and unforgettable.

name: Shadvidhamargini
description: Named for the "six paths." The sharp Ma2 with otherwise moderate notes creates an unusually clear-eyed feeling.

name: Suvarnangi
description: Named "golden-bodied." The flat Ri and Ga with bright upper notes and sharp Ma create a golden, glowing quality.

name: Divyamani
description: Named "divine jewel." The consecutive upper semitones combined with sharp Ma and flat lower register create something genuinely gem-like  ·  brilliant and rare.

name: Dhavalambari
description: Named "white-robed"  ·  the sharp Ma2 and natural Ga3 against flat Ri and flat Da creates a bright, pure quality.

name: Namanarayani
description: Named for saluting Narayana. The Ma2 adds a devotional intensity to the Ri1-Ga3 combination.

name: Kamavardhini
description: Also known as Panthuvarali  ·  the flat Ri beside the sharp Ma2 creates a tension that feels urgent and searching. One of the most frequently performed Ma2 ragas.

name: Ramapriya
description: Named "dear to Rama." The gentle upper tetrachord with bright Ma2 and flat Ri gives a warm, devotional feeling.

name: Gamanashrama
description: The flat Ri1 combined with natural Ga3, sharp Ma2, and bright upper tetrachord creates a striking elevation  ·  like watching a sunrise from a mountaintop ashram.

name: Vishwambhari
description: Named "sustainer of the universe." Consecutive upper semitones with sharp Ma and flat Ri  ·  expansive and all-encompassing in character.

name: Shamalangi
description: Flat Ga2 and flat Da cluster against sharp Ma2  ·  the combination creates a mysteriously beautiful, twilight feeling.

name: Shanmukhapriya
description: Named for Shanmukha (Murugan). Widely used in film music  ·  its Ma2 against Ga2 gives it a vivid, almost cinematic quality. One of the more recognizable Ma2 ragas.

name: Simhendramadhyamam
description: Named "lion in the middle"  ·  the sharp Ma2 and sharp Ni3 against flat Ga2 and flat Da1 gives it a bold, contrasting strength.

name: Hemavati
description: Named for golden snow (Hema = gold). The Ma2 brings a warmth to what would otherwise be a pensive scale.

name: Dharmavati
description: Named for righteousness (dharma). The Ma2 and Ni3 over flat Ga2 creates a firm, principled, clear quality.

name: Neetimati
description: Named "one who has ethics." Consecutive upper semitones with sharp Ma  ·  a raga of principled, deliberate movement.

name: Kantamani
description: Named "gem jewel." Bright Ga3 and sharp Ma2 against flat Da cluster  ·  vivid and glittering.

name: Rishabhapriya
description: Named "dear to Rishaba" (Nandi, Shiva's vehicle). Natural Ga3 with sharp Ma2 and flat Da  ·  graceful and noble.

name: Latangi
description: Named for a graceful woman (latangi). Natural Ga3 and Ni3 with sharp Ma2 and flat Da creates a striking, elegant quality.

name: Vachaspati
description: Named for Brihaspati, the god of wisdom and speech. Natural Ga3 with sharp Ma2 and gentle upper notes  ·  articulate and wise.

name: Mechakalyani
description: The luminous parent of Kalyani  ·  the sharpened Ma2 gives everything a soaring, golden-evening quality. One of the most performed Melakartas, especially at dusk.

name: Chitrambari
description: Named "dressed in pictures"  ·  the consecutive upper notes with sharp Ma2 and natural Ga3 create a vivid, richly ornamented feeling.

name: Sucharitra
description: Named "one with good character." The compressed lower register with sharp Ma2 and flat Da cluster  ·  rare and characterful.

name: Jyotiswarupini
description: Named "embodiment of light." Sharp Ma2 against the compressed lower tetrachord creates a luminous quality  ·  light in the darkness.

name: Dhatuvardani
description: Named "increaser of minerals/elements." The sharp Ni3 and Ma2 over flat lower notes create a sense of growth and elemental force.

name: Nasikabhushani
description: Named for a nose ornament  ·  delicate and precise. The compressed lower tetrachord with gentle upper notes and sharp Ma2 has a fineness to it.

name: Kosalam
description: Named for the ancient kingdom of Kosala (Rama's birthplace). Bright upper notes over the compressed lower tetrachord convey a regal, ancient grandeur.

name: Rasikapriya
description: The 72nd and final Melakarta  ·  "dear to the connoisseur." Consecutive semitone pairs in both registers with sharp Ma2: the raga that rewards careful listening. A fitting end to the complete system.

name: Mohanam
description: Pentatonic and universally beloved  ·  this is the raga people hum without knowing it. Pure joy, wonder, and the sweetness of longing from a distance.

name: Hamsadhwani
description: The swan's voice. Bright, auspicious, and joyful  ·  played at the start of concerts and ceremonies. Vatapi Ganapatim makes this raga sing for everyone who hears it.

name: Bilahari
description: A radiant raga with a direct pentatonic ascent and a fuller descent. The missing Ma and Ni on the way up give Bilahari lift, while the descent restores them for a rounded, joyful return.

name: Sahana
description: Patience and endurance  ·  that's what sahana means. A raga of quiet strength, love that persists despite difficulty.

name: Kalyana Vasantham
description: Spring-time bliss  ·  a joyful, rare pentatonic ascending that skips notes in surprising ways. The kind of raga that makes you smile immediately.

name: Bowli
description: A classic early morning raga. Invokes waking up to fresh morning dew and temple bells. Famous for MS Subbulakshmi's Sriman Narayana.

name: Malahari
description: A gentle morning raga traditionally used for early geethams. Its pentatonic ascent is simple and stable, while Ga3 appears only in the descent, giving the return phrase its characteristic color.

name: Bhairavi
description: A raga that holds entire lifetimes of emotion. Bhairavi is sung at the end of concerts as a farewell  ·  because once you've heard it, nothing else needs to be said.

name: Kamboji
description: A raga of temples and processions  ·  heroic devotion, the feeling of walking toward something sacred. The avarohanam's Ni2 (vakra) is its signature fingerprint.

name: Todi
description: The raga of early mornings and deep feeling. Todi holds sadness beautifully  ·  not wallowing in it, but sitting with it until it becomes something like peace.

name: Saveri
description: Ancient and compassionate  ·  Saveri's pentatonic ascent feels simple until you realise how much it says with so few notes. A beautiful derivative of Mayamalavagowla.

name: Hindolam
description: Five notes and a universe of feeling. Hindolam is the raga of deep night and unresolved longing  ·  sung after midnight, when everything is quiet and the heart speaks.

name: Madhyamavati
description: A majestic pentatonic scale (Audava) that traditionally concludes concerts. Its open fifths and skipping of Ga and Da create a sense of deep stability and resolution. One of the most auspicious ragas in the system.

name: Abheri
description: A raga for still waters  ·  peaceful, devotional, clear. Nagumomu Ganaleni is one of the most beloved Carnatic compositions, and Abheri carries it perfectly.

name: Abhogi
description: A deeply emotive asymmetric pentatonic scale missing Pa and Ni. Without the stabilizing fifth (Pa), Abhogi feels restless and reaching, making it perfect for intense devotional pleading.

name: Kapi
description: A highly expressive, bhava-rich raga with vakra movement and bhasanga color. The ascent commonly uses Ni3 while the descent leans on Ni2, giving Kapi its distinctive emotional pull.

name: Durga
description: Five bright notes  ·  Durga is used in auspicious settings because of its bright, open quality. Close to the Western pentatonic major scale that appears in folk music across the world.

name: Revati
description: Simple, pentatonic, and quietly beautiful. Revati doesn't demand  ·  it simply settles in the ear like evening light.

name: Margahindolam
description: The avarohanam skips Sa's Ri entirely, giving it a characteristically smooth, rolling descent. Gentle and inward, like a slow morning walk to the temple. There is no youtube video of the arohanam and avarohanam but this video shares some notes in the raagam.
